hints.title: Sorting Events Temporally
hints.text: Sort friends by their arrival times, associating each friend with their original index.

hints.title: Tracking Available and Occupied Chairs
hints.text: Maintain an ordered container of currently available chair numbers, and another container of occupied chairs ordered by departure time.

hints.title: Releasing Chairs Prior to Seating
hints.text: Before assigning a chair to an arriving friend, return all chairs occupied by friends whose departure time is less than or equal to arrival.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def smallestChair(self, times: list[list[int]], targetFriend: int) -> int:
        events = []
        for i, (arr, leave) in enumerate(times):
            events.append((arr, leave, i))
        events.sort()
        
        available_chairs = list(range(len(times)))
        heapq.heapify(available_chairs)
        leaving_heap = []
        
        for arr, leave, i in events:
            while leaving_heap and leaving_heap[0][0] <= arr:
                _, chair = heapq.heappop(leaving_heap)
                heapq.heappush(available_chairs, chair)
                
            assigned_chair = heapq.heappop(available_chairs)
            if i == targetFriend:
                return assigned_chair
            heapq.heappush(leaving_heap, (leave, assigned_chair))
        return -1
```

complexity.notes: Two priority structures managing available chair numbers and pending release times.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning all chairs linearly for the minimum available index takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual heaps process chair allocations and releases in logarithmic time per arrival.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should coordinate two priority heaps (available chair IDs and departure timestamps).
